where it is correctly written enclitically in M (ὥσφας [as them]), while in others it is often σφάς [them] or σφᾶς [them]. Apollonius on the pronoun p. 387 (127) posits two forms, one σφας [them], of which the Ionic resolution is σφέας [them], the other σφας [them] enclitic, with the alpha shortened. If we follow this rule, in Sophocles Ant. 128, where in the anapestic dipody σφας [them] is long, we should not write with the Laurentian manuscript καί σφας ἐσιδών [and seeing them], but καὶ σφᾶς [and them], while the enclitic σφάς [them] is to be approved in the remaining places, as I said in the Lexicon Sophocleum p. 229.
On the singular accusative ope and the dative plural σφίσιν [to them] and σφιν [to them] see above p. 161.

Hesychius: σφυδῶν: ἰσχυρός, εὔρωστος, σκληρός [strong, vigorous, hard], and διασφυδῶσαι: αὐξῆσαι, ἀπὸ τοῦ σφύζειν [to cause to swell: to increase, from to throb], from σφυδόω [to be full], of which form an example is ἐσφυδωμένοι [swollen] in Timocles ap. Athen. 6 p. 246 f., meaning replete, turgid, distended after devouring food abundantly, as Schweigh. translates.
